Use gpt-6-astra xhigh. Offline analysis only: do not modify code/artifacts, no board/UART/USB/Windows/network/credentials. Goal remains numbered xTS filesystem/Wi-Fi optimization, no unsafe tradeoffs; latest user says default S31 ESP-IDF reference and stop sufficient directions. Read backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-idf-default-baseline/{README.md,root-reviewed-statistics.json}, current checklist and capability matrix as needed.
Need decisive next board baseline choice and narrow guidance, not a new broad plan. Root proposes use frozen E87 backlog1 paired build on CURRENT AP60:ce:41:ab:02:d0/ch11, host192.168.1.29 (IDF just succeeded), original59440/etc cases, 30s, pinned old EXE73096a...a4cd. E69 lacks backlog while -C server uses select before accept; E87 adds backlog1+bounded diagnostics but failed on oldAP/ch6. Review actual source and current evidence to decide E87 vsE69 for same-AP baseline, and whether original5471 diagnostic remains next only if TCPRXfails. Can all4directions be run without invalid RX gating hiding independent TX/UDP evidence, while safely restoringafterfailure? Focus causal/quality limitations, no arbitrary speedbudget. Existing return-path analysis: korvo-tcp-listener-backlog/connection-return-path-analysis.md. Send concise result, source pointers and concrete blockers. All hardware/transport Root only. Avoid redundant giant audits or new tests unless specific defect. You may create only a concise guidance.md under backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-default-reference-followup if useful; no changes elsewhere.

I’ll review the frozen builds, runner control flow, and existing evidence offline, then give a narrow baseline recommendation with source pointers. I’ll use a delegated GPT-6 Astra review at xhigh as requested; all hardware and transport actions remain with Root.
I’m using the xTS board evidence skill to keep the review tied to the paired firmware and original case evidence. This review will remain offline and read-only.

The evidence favors E87 for the next baseline: E69’s successful RX run omitted `-C`, so it did not exercise the required select-before-accept path. The existing E87 runner blocks TX after invalid RX and covers only TCP; the remaining check is how to preserve independent direction results while keeping cleanup and restoration mandatory.

The blockers are in the runner: it still pins the old AP/channel, and its restoration-proof reader expects a layout that the latest IDF transaction does not use. A follow-up must also distinguish an invalid throughput result from unsafe cleanup state—only the latter should prevent independent directions from running.

The narrow recommendation is unchanged: run E87 at the original ports on the current AP, and reserve 5471 for a reproduced TCP RX connection/listener failure. “All four directions” means four independent attempts when cleanup is verified; it must not mean continuing through a reset, timeout, or unconfirmed process cleanup.

**Choose frozen E87 for the current-AP baseline**, using paired kernel `aa46557c…f5786` / AppFS `31452f8b…34d34`. GPT-6 Astra at xhigh completed the requested offline review; no files or hardware were changed.

E87 is the appropriate baseline because `-C` executes [select before accept](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-tcp-listener-backlog/source/openvela-dev/external/iperf2/iperf2/src/Listener.cpp:193). Before accept registers its callback, connection handoff requires the [backlog branch](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-tcp-listener-backlog/source/openvela-dev/nuttx/net/tcp/tcp_listen.c:285), disabled in E69. E69’s successful historical RX omitted `-C`. E87’s old-AP failure establishes neither completed handshake nor lost poll notification.

Use AP **60:ce:41:ab:02:d0/ch11**, host **192.168.1.29**, pinned EXE **73096a…a4cd**, and 30 seconds. Preserve both endpoints’ `-C`, board window 64000 B, TCP block 16384 B, UDP 1470 B/40M, and host default window. The IDF comparison ports are **59440 / 59441 / 59442 / 5001**—UDP TX uses 5001.

**All four directions can produce independent evidence, but the existing runner cannot be used unchanged.** Concrete blockers:

- **Invalid RX gates TX:** [GatedHost](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-tcp-listener-backlog/board-tools/run_board.py:49) rejects every host server when TCP RX is unusable; extending it unchanged would also suppress UDP TX. Select all four cases and gate continuation on verified cleanup and board health. A failed measurement must retain its own failure without hiding later directions.
- **Cleanup verification is insufficient:** the inherited [exception path](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-network-idf-comparison/board-tools-v2/e69_loop.py:393) can swallow kill errors. Confirm owned board tasks and host workers have exited before continuing. Timeout, reset, lost responsiveness, or unconfirmed cleanup must stop remaining traffic.
- **Environment/proof assumptions are stale:** [AP constants](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-network-idf-comparison/board-tools-v2/tx_profile.py:39) still select ch6. The [proof reader](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-network-idf-comparison/board-tools-v2/run_board.py:46) expects `transaction/plan.json`; latest IDF evidence uses top-level `plan.json` and a schema E87 rejects. Support that actual format while preserving identity, freshness and full-byte checks. The temporary C-path EXE was also removed; Root must restore its verified placement before execution.

Preserve outer-finally restoration and full 16 MiB verification. [Recovery](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-network-idf-comparison/board-tools-v2/run_board.py:130) blocks reset if owned-host cleanup fails, so that condition must remain explicitly **recovery incomplete**. Any no-client check should reuse the same UART session; reopening previously caused a reset.

**5471 remains conditional:** use it only if original 59440 again fails connection/readiness. Its existing SYN-ACK diagnostics and bounded ARP/TCP snapshots can narrow the [unresolved return path](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-tcp-listener-backlog/connection-return-path-analysis.md). A successful but slow RX does not justify this connection diagnostic.

Use the current reference’s approximately **2.8/2.8/25/12 Mbit/s and observed ranges** to stop sufficient directions. Retain actual UDP input, loss/reporting limitations, ACK and recovery quality; never adopt IDF’s large TX sequence gaps. These 30-second measurements do not establish 300-second xTS acceptance.
